Yes, ascitis volume and anthropometric measurements should be estimated in hospitalized alcoholic cirrhotics. 

Estimating ascitis volume can help assess the severity of liver disease and guide treatment, such as paracentesis (fluid removal) to relieve discomfort and prevent complications. 

Anthropometric measurements, such as body mass index (BMI), mid-arm muscle circumference, and triceps skinfold, can help evaluate the patient's nutritional status, which is often compromised in alcoholic cirrhosis. Malnutrition is common in these patients and can worsen prognosis, so assessing and addressing nutritional deficiencies is crucial. 

Regular monitoring of these parameters can also help track the patient's response to treatment and identify potential complications early on.
